meanings: (bound form) Japan (abbr. for 日本[Ri4 ben3])
etymologyHint: The sun

components.note: 日 depicts the sun as a circle with a dot or short stroke inside — a simplified picture of the sun's disc, later squared off in the standard script.

example.hanzi: 日出的时候,天空是红色的。
example.pinyin: Rìchū de shíhou, tiānkōng shì hóngsè de.
example.english: The sky is red at sunrise.
example.fact: Sunrise skies often look red or orange because sunlight scatters more when the sun is low on the horizon — the same reason sunsets are colorful.

etymologyHint: Soldiers 冖 (distorted 力) in a cart 车

components.note: 冖 here is a distorted form of 力 (strength) — a simplified way of showing soldiers grouped together.
车 (cart/vehicle) — 军 originally pictured soldiers riding out to battle in war chariots.

example.pinyin: Tā de bàba zài jūnduì gōngzuò.
example.english: His dad works in the military.
example.fact: War chariots were an important part of Chinese armies more than 3,000 years ago, during the Shang and Zhou dynasties.

meanings: (after a verb or adjective) one who (is) ...

example.hanzi: 这本书的作者是中国人。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū de zuòzhě shì Zhōngguó rén.
example.fact: 者 attaches to a verb or noun to mean 'the one who does it,' similar to '-er' in English — as in 作者 (writer) or 读者 (reader).

meanings: (bound form) intention; feeling; inclination; state of mind
etymologyHint: heart

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 意 relates to thought, intention, and meaning, things of the mind.
音 (yīn) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading has drifted from yì, though both share a similar vowel.

example.english: Mom agreed to let me go to the park.
example.fact: 意 appears in many everyday words about thinking, such as 同意 (to agree), 主意 (an idea), and 意思 (meaning).

meanings: used in 南無|南无[na1 mo2]

example.fact: 无 means 'without' or 'nothing' and is common in literary Chinese; in everyday speech 没有 is usually used instead, though 无 survives in words like 无聊 (bored) and 无论 (no matter what).

etymologyHint: A plow's head representing strength

components.note: 力 depicts the blade of a plow — since plowing fields took great physical effort, the shape came to represent strength or power.

example.fact: 力 means 'strength' or 'power' and appears in many common words, such as 努力 (to work hard) and 力量 (strength, force).

example.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de māo, tā hěn kě'ài.
example.english: This is my cat, it is very cute.
example.fact: 它 is the pronoun 'it,' used for animals and objects — Chinese has separate characters for 'he' (他), 'she' (她), and 'it' (它), all pronounced the same tā.

example.pinyin: Zhōngguó yǔ Měiguó dōu shì dàguó.
example.english: China and the US are both large countries.
example.fact: 与 means 'and' or 'with' and is common in written and formal Chinese; in casual speech, 和 is used instead.

etymologyHint: Simplified form of 長; an old man with long hair and a cane

components.note: 长 (simplified from 長) depicts an elderly figure with long flowing hair and a cane — length and seniority are linked in the original picture.

example.pinyin: Xiǎo háizi hěn kuài jiù zhǎngdà le.
example.fact: 长 has two pronunciations: zhǎng, meaning 'to grow' or 'chief' (as in 校长, principal), and cháng, meaning 'long' (as in 长城, the Great Wall).

meanings: to hold a baby in position to help it urinate or defecate
etymologyHint: hand

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 把 relates to grasping or holding something with the hand.
巴 (bā) gives the sound — 把 is pronounced bǎ, a close match differing only in tone.

example.fact: 把 is a versatile character — it can be a measure word for objects with handles (一把伞, an umbrella) or introduce the 把-construction, one of the most distinctive sentence patterns in Chinese grammar.

etymologyHint: A table 几 made of wood 木; 几 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 木 (wood) — 机 originally referred to a wooden device or machine, such as a loom.
几 depicts a small table or stool — combined with 木 (wood), the character pictured a wooden machine or mechanism.

example.english: I use my phone to make a call.
example.fact: 机 originally meant a wooden loom or mechanical device; today it appears in modern inventions like 手机 (cellphone) and 飞机 (airplane).
Chinese numbers follow a simple base-ten pattern — eleven is 十一 (ten-one), twelve is 十二 (ten-two), and twenty is 二十 (two-ten), making counting very regular compared to English.

etymologyHint: An eye 巳 pierced by a dagger 戈, an old mark of slavery

components.note: 巳 (here representing an eye) — in one traditional theory, this depicted a captive's marked eye, an ancient sign of subjugation, which later broadened to mean 'the common people.'
戈 (a dagger-axe) — combined with the eye shape above, this ties the character to the idea of marking or piercing.

example.fact: China officially recognizes 56 ethnic groups, with the Han majority alongside groups such as Tibetan, Uyghur, and Zhuang.

meanings: (prefix indicating ordinal number, as in 第六[di4 liu4] "sixth")
(literary) grades in which successful candidates in the imperial examinations were placed
etymologyHint: Bamboo strips ⺮ arrayed in sequence; 弟 provides the pronunciation

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — ancient texts were written on bound bamboo strips, and 第 originally referred to the sequential order of such strips, giving rise to its meaning 'ordinal number' (as in 第一, first).

example.english: He is number one / first place.
example.fact: 第 turns numbers into ordinals, similar to '-th' in English — 第一 is 'first,' 第二 is 'second,' and so on.

etymologyHint: To divide 八 what is private 厶

components.note: 八 here depicts something splitting apart or being divided.
厶 is an old form meaning 'private' or 'one's own' — 公 shows dividing up private property to share it fairly, giving rise to the meaning 'public' or 'fair.'

example.english: He goes to the company to work every day.
example.fact: 公 means 'public' or 'fair' and appears in many everyday words, such as 公司 (company), 公园 (park), and 公共 (public).

etymologyHint: sitting man

components.note: 匕 here relates to a person crouching or sitting — 此 originally pictured 'this place' where someone is.
止 (zhǐ) gives a hint of the sound — 此 is pronounced cǐ, sharing a similar final though the initial has shifted over time.

example.fact: 此 is a formal word for 'this,' often seen in writing — as in 因此 (therefore) and 此外 (besides) — while 这 is used for 'this' in everyday speech.
已 means 'already' and most often appears in 已经, one of the most common ways to show that something has already happened.

etymologyHint: A spade or other workman's tool

components.note: 工 depicts a carpenter's square or workman's tool — a simple shape that came to represent work and labor.

example.english: Dad goes to work every day.
example.fact: 工 means 'work' or 'labor' and combines with 作 to form 工作 (job, to work), one of the most frequently used words in daily Chinese.

etymologyHint: A person 亻 working for the government 吏

components.note: 亻 (person) — 使 involves a person carrying out a task.
吏 (a government official) — 使 originally referred to an official sent to carry out orders, giving rise to the meaning 'to make someone do something' or 'to use.'

example.english: Using a cellphone is very convenient.
example.fact: 使 can mean 'to use' (使用) or 'to make/cause someone to do something,' a common causative pattern in Chinese grammar.

etymologyHint: heart

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 情 is pronounced qíng, a close match differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Jīntiān tā de xīnqíng hěn hǎo.
example.english: Today his mood is very good.
example.fact: 情 relates to feelings and appears in words like 心情 (mood), 感情 (emotion, affection), and 爱情 (romantic love).

etymologyHint: The light of the sun 日 and moon 月

components.note: 日 (sun) — combined with 月 (moon), 明 shows the light of both sun and moon, giving the meaning 'bright' or 'clear.'
月 (moon) — together with 日 (sun), the two brightest things in the sky represent brightness and clarity.

example.fact: 明 means 'bright' and appears in 明天 (tomorrow, literally 'bright day') and 聪明 (clever, intelligent).

etymologyHint: heart

components.note: 忄 (heart/mind) — 性 relates to inner nature or character.
生 (shēng) gives a hint of the sound — 性 is pronounced xìng, a related sound though the initial has shifted.

example.fact: 性 relates to inherent nature and appears in words like 性格 (personality) and 女性/男性 (female/male).

etymologyHint: mouth

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 知 relates to speaking what one knows.
矢 (shǐ) gives a hint of the sound — 知 is pronounced zhī, a connection that has faded over time.

example.fact: 知 means 'to know' and is most commonly seen in 知道 (zhīdào), one of the first verbs beginners learn.

etymologyHint: Jade 玉 put away 入 for safe-keeping

components.note: 入 (enter, put away) — 全 pictures something being placed into safekeeping.
玉 (jade) — a valuable treasure kept whole and undamaged, giving 全 its meaning of 'complete' or 'entire.'

example.pinyin: Tā quánbù dōu chī wán le.
example.fact: 全 means 'whole' or 'complete' and appears in 完全 (completely) and 全部 (all, the whole).

etymologyHint: Three  parallel lines; compare 一 (one) and 二 (two)

components.note: 三 is made of three simple horizontal strokes stacked together — the most direct way to picture the number three, following the same pattern as 一 (one) and 二 (two).

example.fact: Traffic lights use the same three colors almost everywhere in the world: red, yellow, and green.

etymologyHint: A right hand, representing a pair; compare 左

components.note: 又 is a simplified picture of a right hand — later used to mean 'again' or 'also,' perhaps from the idea of doing something 'once more' with one's hand.

example.fact: 又 means 'again' or 'also,' often used to show a repeated or additional action, as in 又来了 (came again).

meanings: to close; to shut; to turn off

example.fact: 关 means 'to close' (关门, close the door) and also 'related to' (关系, relationship, and 有关, related to).

etymologyHint: fire

components.note: 灬 (fire) — 点 originally related to a small flame or dot of light, giving rise to the meaning 'dot' or 'point.'
占 (zhàn) gives a hint of the sound — 点 is pronounced diǎn, a connection that has drifted over the centuries.

example.fact: 点 is used to tell time in Chinese — 三点 means '3 o'clock,' literally 'three points' on the clock face.

meanings: first month of the lunar year
etymologyHint: A foot 止 stopping in the right place 一

components.note: 一 (a line, representing a target or standard) — 正 shows a foot arriving exactly at the right mark.
止 (foot, to stop) — arriving and stopping precisely at the target gives 正 its meaning of 'correct' or 'straight.'

example.fact: 正 means 'correct' or 'exactly,' and 正在 marks an action happening right now, similar to '-ing' in English.
业 relates to work or study and appears in 作业 (homework), 工业 (industry), and 毕业 (to graduate).

etymologyHint: Night-time 夕 divinations 卜; the supernatural, the foreign

components.note: 夕 (evening, night) — divination was traditionally done in the evening.
卜 (to divine, reading cracks in bone or shell) — combined with 夕 (evening), an evening divination was for unusual or 'outside' matters, giving 外 its meaning of 'outside' or 'foreign.'

example.fact: 外 means 'outside' or 'foreign' and appears in words like 外面 (outside), 外国 (foreign country), and 国外 (abroad).

etymologyHint: Going to bed 丬 at night 夕, a predictable future

components.note: 丬 (a stylized bed) — 将 originally pictured someone preparing for bed at night.
夕 (evening/night) — the coming of night was seen as predictable, giving 将 its meaning 'about to' or 'going to' happen.

example.english: In the future, he wants to be a doctor.
example.fact: 将 means 'about to' or 'the future,' as in 将来 (jiānglái, the future) and 将要 (about to).

etymologyHint: Two people 从 together in a cart

components.note: 冂 (a covering or frame, here representing a cart) — 两 pictures two things sharing one enclosure.
从 (two people following each other) — together with the frame above, 两 shows a pair joined together, giving its meaning 'two' or 'both.'

example.fact: 两 and 二 both mean 'two,' but 两 is used before measure words (两个, two of something) while 二 is used in counting and numbers like 12 or 22.

etymologyHint: A tall palace

components.note: 高 depicts a tall tower or palace, with a roof at the top and a base below — a simple picture of height.

example.fact: 珠穆朗玛峰 (Mount Everest) is the tallest mountain in the world, standing on the border between China and Nepal.

etymologyHint: The sun 日 shining through a doorway 门

components.note: 门 (door/gate) — 间 pictures light passing through an entryway.
日 (sun) — sunlight shining through a gap in a doorway gave 间 its meaning of a space 'in between,' as in 中间 (in the middle) or 时间 (time, the space between moments).

example.fact: 间 means 'a space between' and appears in 时间 (time), 房间 (room), and 中间 (the middle).

etymologyHint: Road 丨 leading to the farm 田

components.note: 由 resembles 田 (a field) with a stem or road extending from it — pointing the way toward a source, which gave 由 its meaning of 'from' or 'cause.'

example.fact: 由 means 'from' or 'due to,' and appears in words like 自由 (freedom, literally 'from oneself') and 理由 (reason).

etymologyHint: mouth

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 问 relates to speaking, specifically asking a question.
门 (mén) gives a hint of the sound — 问 is pronounced wèn, related but the tone and vowel have shifted.

example.english: Excuse me, where is the restroom?
example.fact: 问 means 'to ask' and 请问 (may I ask) is one of the most common polite phrases for starting a question.

meanings: (also, often used before an adjective without intensifying its meaning, i.e. as a meaningless syntactic element)
etymologyHint: step

components.note: 彳 (step, to walk) — an older, now faded connection tied to movement.
艮 (gèn) gives a hint of the sound — 很 is pronounced hěn, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.

example.fact: 很 means 'very' and is one of the most common intensifiers in Chinese, used before adjectives like 好 (good) or 大 (big).

meanings: (before an adjective or verb) to the highest degree; (the) most ...; -est
etymologyHint: To take place 取 under the sun 日 (that is, everywhere)

components.note: 日 (sun) — 最 pictures something happening under the sun, that is, everywhere.
取 (to take, gather) — combined with the sun above, gathering everything under the sun gave 最 its meaning of 'most' or 'the utmost.'

example.hanzi: 长江是中国最长的河流。
example.pinyin: Chángjiāng shì Zhōngguó zuì cháng de héliú.
example.english: The Yangtze is China's longest river.
example.fact: 最 forms superlatives, similar to '-est' in English — 最长 means 'longest,' and the Yangtze River is the longest river in both China and Asia.

etymologyHint: A burden carried for a thousand 千 miles 里

components.note: 千 (thousand) — 重 pictures a heavy burden carried a great distance.
里 (a unit of distance, like a mile) — carrying something a thousand 里 emphasizes how heavy and significant a burden it is, giving 重 its meaning 'heavy' or 'important.'

example.fact: 重 means 'heavy' and also 'important' — the same character gives us both 很重 (very heavy) and 重要 (important).

etymologyHint: Simplified form of 並; two men standing side-by-side

components.note: 并 (simplified from 並) depicts two people standing side by side — giving its meaning of 'together' or 'and.'

example.hanzi: 这个方法简单并且有效。
example.english: This method is simple and effective.
example.fact: 并 means 'together' and often connects two ideas, as in 并且 (moreover, and also).

meanings: (literary) the outside world as distinct from oneself; people other than oneself
etymologyHint: ox

components.note: 牛 (ox/cattle) — cattle were among the earliest and most valuable kinds of property, connecting 物 to the general idea of 'object' or 'thing.'
勿 (wù) gives the sound — 物 is also pronounced wù, an exact match.

example.fact: 物 means 'thing' and appears in 动物 (animal, literally 'moving thing'), 植物 (plant), and 购物 (shopping).

meanings: person engaged in certain types of work
person skilled in certain types of work
etymologyHint: A hand with the fingers splayed

components.note: 手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

example.english: You should wash your hands before eating.
example.fact: 手 means 'hand' and appears in many everyday words, such as 手机 (cellphone, literally 'hand machine') and 洗手 (to wash hands).
应 in 应该 (yīnggāi, should) is pronounced with the 1st tone yīng; the same character is also read yìng (4th tone) in words like 应用 (application) and 反应 (reaction) — a common tone trap for learners.

etymologyHint: spear

components.note: 戈 (a dagger-axe, a weapon) — 战 relates to fighting and war.
占 (zhàn) gives the sound — 战 is also pronounced zhàn, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 长城很长。它帮助中国防止战争。
example.pinyin: Chángchéng hěn cháng. Tā bāngzhù Zhōngguó fángzhǐ zhànzhēng.
example.english: The Great Wall is very long. It helped China prevent wars.
example.fact: 长城 (the Great Wall of China) was built over many centuries to help defend against invasions from the north.
向 means 'toward' and shows direction, as in 向右 (to the right) and 向前 (forward).

etymologyHint: high

components.note: 大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.

example.fact: 头 means 'head' and also means 'first' or 'leader' in words like 头等 (first-class) and 队头 (head of a line).

etymologyHint: A tattooed chest, representing writing

components.note: 文 depicts a chest marked with crossing lines, once tattoos or patterns on the body — decoration and pattern gave rise to the idea of 'writing' and 'culture.'

example.fact: 文 means 'writing' or 'culture' and appears in 中文 (the Chinese language) and 文化 (culture).

meanings: used in 體己|体己[ti1 ji5]

example.english: Exercise is very good for the body.
example.fact: 体 means 'body' and most often appears in 身体 (the body) and 体育 (physical education, sports).

etymologyHint: script

components.note: 攵 (a hand with a stick, action) — 政 relates to administering or governing.
正 (zhèng) gives the sound — 政 is also pronounced zhèng, an exact match.

example.fact: 政 relates to governing and politics; 政府 means 'government,' which for China is based in Beijing.

meanings: (bound form) the Americas (abbr. for 美洲[Mei3 zhou1])
(bound form) USA (abbr. for 美國|美国[Mei3 guo2])
etymologyHint: A person 大 wearing an elegant crown 羊

components.note: 羊 (sheep; here representing feathers or ornaments on a headdress) — an elaborate decoration worn on the head.
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — a person wearing a decorated headdress was seen as beautiful, giving 美 its meaning 'beautiful.'

example.english: The scenery here is very beautiful.
example.fact: 美 means 'beautiful' and is also used as a short form for 美国 (the United States, literally 'beautiful country').

etymologyHint: To stare 目 at a tree 木, meaning to observe

components.note: 木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'

example.hanzi: 朋友之间应该互相帮助。
example.fact: 相 often means 'mutual' or 'each other,' as in 互相 (each other) and 相信 (to believe/trust).

etymologyHint: Simplified form of 見; a man 儿 with the eye 目 emphasized

components.note: 冂 (a simplified eye shape in 见's modern form) — emphasizes the act of seeing.
儿 (a person) — a person with an emphasized eye above gives 见 its meaning 'to see.'

example.fact: 见 means 'to see' and 再见 (literally 'see again') is the standard way to say goodbye in Chinese.

meanings: used to indicate passive voice (placed before the doer of the action like "by" in English passive-voice sentences, or, if the doer is not mentioned, before the verb)
(since c. 2009) (sarcastic or jocular) used to indicate that the following word should be regarded as being in air quotes (as in 被旅遊|被旅游[bei4 lu : 3 you2] to "go on a trip")
etymologyHint: cloth

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — 被 originally meant a quilt or covering, like a blanket.
皮 (pí) gives a hint of the sound — 被 is pronounced bèi, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.pinyin: Bēizi bèi xiǎo māo dǎpò le.
example.english: The cup was broken by the kitten.
example.fact: 被 marks the passive voice in Chinese, similar to 'was/were done by' in English, as in 被打破 (was broken).

etymologyHint: Harvesting 刂 grain 禾

components.note: 禾 (grain, a growing rice or wheat plant) — 利 pictures a harvest.
刂 (knife) — cutting grain at harvest time was a clear benefit or gain, giving 利 its meaning 'profit' or 'advantage.'

example.english: We should use our time to study.
example.fact: 利 means 'benefit' or 'profit' and appears in 利用 (to make use of) and 有利 (favorable, beneficial).

meanings: ten (used in fractions, writing checks etc)
etymologyHint: A file of ten 十 people 亻

components.note: 亻 (person) — 什 originally referred to a group of people.
十 (ten) — combined with 亻 (person), 什 originally described a group of ten; the character later came to be used for the common word 什么 (what).

example.fact: 什 is almost always seen in 什么 (shénme, what), one of the first question words beginners learn.

etymologyHint: Two  parallel lines; compare 一 (one) and 三 (three)

components.note: 二 is simply two horizontal strokes stacked together — the most direct way to picture the number two, following the same pattern as 一 (one) and 三 (three).

example.fact: 二 means 'two' and is used in math and counting, though 两 is used instead of 二 before measure words, as in 两个人 (two people).

meanings: and so on; etc.; et al.
etymologyHint: Bamboo strips ⺮ laid before a court 寺

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — 等 pictures bamboo strips, once used as writing tablets, being sorted.
寺 (originally a government office, later 'temple') — sorting and arranging bamboo documents at an official court gave 等 its meanings 'to wait,' 'rank,' and 'etc.'

example.fact: 等 means 'to wait' and also 'and so on' (等等), used the way English uses 'etc.'

components.note: 厂 (chǎng) gives a hint of the sound — 产 is pronounced chǎn, nearly identical apart from the final consonant.

example.english: China produces a lot of tea.
example.fact: 产 means 'to produce' and appears in 生产 (to produce, production) and 产品 (product).

etymologyHint: To defend yourself 口 with a spear 戈; "or else"

components.note: 戈 (a spear or weapon) — 或 pictures defending a territory.
口 (here representing a walled area or territory) — defending one's territory with a weapon gave 或 its early sense of 'a certain place,' which later shifted to mean 'or,' offering an alternative.

example.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng hē chá huòzhě kāfēi?
example.english: Do you want to drink tea or coffee?
example.fact: 或 means 'or,' most often seen in 或者 (huòzhě), used to offer a choice between two things.

meanings: abbr. for Xinjiang 新疆[Xin1 jiang1]
abbr. for Singapore 新加坡[Xin1 jia1 po1]
etymologyHint: A freshly chopped 斤 tree 亲

components.note: 亲 (here representing a tree, related to 榛/hazel) — 新 pictures a tree being cut.
斤 (an axe) — freshly chopping wood gave 新 its meaning of something 'new' or 'fresh.'

example.fact: 新 means 'new' and appears in 新年 (New Year) and 新闻 (news, literally 'new hearing').

meanings: sixth of the ten Heavenly Stems 十天干[shi2 tian1 gan1]
etymologyHint: A loom woven with thread

components.note: 己 is thought to depict a woven cord or thread pattern, though its exact original picture is debated; it came to be used for the reflexive idea of 'oneself.'

example.english: He likes to eat by himself.
example.fact: 己 means 'oneself' and almost always appears in 自己 (zìjǐ), one of the most common ways to say 'oneself' in Chinese.

etymologyHint: knife

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 制 relates to cutting and shaping, and by extension, to making or controlling something.
巾 (jīn) gives a hint of the sound — 制 is pronounced zhì, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 这个手表是在中国制作的。
example.pinyin: Zhège shǒubiǎo shì zài Zhōngguó zhìzuò de.
example.english: This watch was made in China.
example.fact: 制 means 'to make' or 'to control' and appears in 制作 (to make) and 制度 (a system).

etymologyHint: A pregnant woman

components.note: 身 depicts a person's torso, originally showing a pregnant woman's body — later broadened to mean 'the body' in general.

example.pinyin: Tā de shēngāo yì mǐ bā.
example.fact: 身 means 'body' and appears in 身体 (the body) and 身高 (height, literally 'body height').

etymologyHint: Fruit 田 growing on a tree 木

components.note: 田 (here representing round fruit, not its usual meaning 'field') — 果 pictures fruit hanging from branches.
木 (tree) — fruit growing on a tree gave 果 its meaning 'fruit' and, more broadly, 'result.'

example.fact: 果 means 'fruit' and also 'result' — 水果 means fruit, while 结果 means the result or outcome of something.

meanings: Canada (abbr. for 加拿大[Jia1 na2 da4])
etymologyHint: Supporting a cause with the strength 力 of one's words 口

components.note: 力 (strength) — 加 pictures adding one's effort to a cause.
口 (mouth, words) — combining strength with words of support gave 加 its meaning 'to add' or 'to increase.'

example.fact: 加 means 'to add,' used in simple math (三加五, three plus five) and in words like 参加 (to participate, literally 'to add oneself in').

meanings: abbr. for Spain 西班牙[Xi1 ban1 ya2]
etymologyHint: A bird settling into its nest, representing sunset; compare 東

components.note: 西 is thought to depict a bird settling into its nest at dusk — since birds return to roost as the sun sets in the west, the character came to mean 'west.'

example.hanzi: 西安是中国古代的首都。
example.pinyin: Xī'ān shì Zhōngguó gǔdài de shǒudū.
example.english: Xi'an was an ancient capital of China.
example.fact: 西安, whose name means 'western peace,' served as the capital of China during several dynasties, including the Tang dynasty.
斯 has little independent meaning today; it mainly appears in phonetic transliterations of foreign names, such as 俄罗斯 (Russia) and 斯里兰卡 (Sri Lanka).

etymologyHint: A crescent moon

components.note: 月 is a simple picture of a crescent moon.

example.pinyin: Jīntiān wǎnshang de yuèliang hěn yuán.
example.fact: 月 means both 'moon' and 'month' — a lunar month was traditionally measured by the moon's cycle from new moon to full moon and back.

etymologyHint: A spoken 讠 tongue 舌; 舌 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 话 relates to speaking and words.
舌 (tongue) — the organ used for speaking, reinforcing 话's meaning of 'speech' or 'words.'

example.fact: 话 means 'speech' or 'words' and appears in 说话 (to speak) and 电话 (telephone, literally 'electric speech').

example.english: This piece of clothing fits well.
example.fact: 合 means 'to combine' or 'to fit,' appearing in 合适 (suitable) and 合作 (to cooperate).

meanings: to go back; to return; to turn back; to turn around
etymologyHint: Originally, a spiral signifying return

components.note: 回 depicts a spiral or winding shape — something that turns back on itself, giving rise to the meaning 'to return.'

example.pinyin: Tā měitiān liù diǎn huí jiā.
example.english: He goes home at six o'clock every day.
example.fact: 回 means 'to return,' and 回家 (to go home) is one of the most common everyday phrases.

etymologyHint: ox

components.note: 牛 (ox) — 特 originally referred to a male ox singled out for sacrifice, a special animal set apart from the herd.
寺 (sì) gives a hint of the sound — 特 is pronounced tè, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de cài hěn tèbié.
example.english: This restaurant's food is very special.
example.fact: 特 means 'special' and appears in 特别 (especially, special) and 特点 (characteristic, feature).

meanings: to be a substitute for; to act on behalf of; to replace; to substitute
generation; dynasty; age; period; (historical) era; (geological) eon
etymologyHint: A man 亻 caught 弋 by the passing of time

components.note: 亻 (person) — 代 relates to a person's place in time.
弋 (a stake used to mark or catch something) — combined with 亻 (person), 代 came to mean a 'generation' or 'era,' and 'to take the place of' someone.

example.english: He represents China in the competition.
example.fact: 代 means 'generation' or 'to take the place of,' appearing in 时代 (era) and 代表 (to represent).

etymologyHint: A man 人  entering a door 冂

components.note: 冂 (an enclosure or doorway) — 内 pictures the space one enters.
人 (person) — a person entering an enclosure gave 内 its meaning 'inside' or 'within.'

example.pinyin: Zhè shì Zhōngguó guónèi de xīnwén.
example.fact: 内 means 'inside' and appears in 国内 (domestic, within the country) and 内部 (interior, internal).
信 means 'to trust' (相信, to believe) and also 'a letter,' as in 写信 (to write a letter).

etymologyHint: Fur 毛 clothing 衣; a shawl or wrap

components.note: 毛 (fur, hair) — 表 originally pictured a fur garment worn on the outside.
衣 (clothing) — an outer fur wrap gave 表 its meaning of 'outer' or 'surface,' and later, 'to express' (showing something on the surface).

example.english: A watch can tell you the time.
example.fact: 表 originally meant an outer garment, and later came to mean 'surface' or 'to express,' as in 表示 (to express) and 手表 (wristwatch, literally 'hand surface').
化 means 'to change' or '-ize,' as in 变化 (change) and 文化 (culture).

meanings: prefix used before the surname of a person or a numeral indicating the order of birth of the children in a family or to indicate affection or familiarity
etymologyHint: A person bent over with long hair 匕 and a crutch; compare 耂

components.note: 耂 (a person bent with age, with long hair) — depicts an elderly figure.
匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.

example.pinyin: Wǒ de lǎoshī rén hěn hǎo.
example.fact: 老 means 'old' and appears in 老师 (teacher, literally 'old master') and 老人 (elderly person).

etymologyHint: thread

components.note: 纟 (thread/silk) — 给 originally related to supplying thread or material, later broadening to mean 'to give.'
合 (hé) gives a hint of the sound — 给 is pronounced gěi, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.pinyin: Tā gěi wǒ yì běn shū.
example.fact: 给 means 'to give' and is also used as a preposition meaning 'for' or 'to,' as in 给我打电话 (call me, give me a call).

etymologyHint: Three leaves on a branch

components.note: 世 depicts three leaves or shoots on a stem, suggesting continuous growth across generations — giving rise to the meaning 'generation' or 'world.'

example.pinyin: Shìjiè shàng yǒu hěn duō yǔyán.
example.english: There are many languages in the world.
example.fact: 世 means 'generation' or 'era' and combines with 界 (boundary) to form 世界 (the world).

etymologyHint: The place where a person 亻 stands 立

components.note: 亻 (person) — 位 relates to a person's location.
立 (to stand) — the spot where a person stands gave 位 its meaning 'position' or 'place,' and later, a polite measure word for people.

example.fact: 位 is a polite measure word used for people, similar to saying 'this gentleman' or 'this lady' — 这位老师 shows extra respect compared to just 这个老师.

etymologyHint: A person 欠 yawning multiple times 冫

components.note: 冫 (originally a mark for repetition, unrelated to its later meaning 'ice') — suggests something done more than once.
欠 (a person yawning, mouth open) — repeated yawning gave 次 its meaning of a 'time' or occurrence, as in counting how many times something happens.

example.english: I have been to China twice.
example.fact: 次 is a measure word for counting occurrences, similar to 'times' in English — 两次 means 'twice.'

etymologyHint: Twenty 廿 people 又 meeting inside a building 广 to deliberate

components.note: 广 (a building or shelter) — 度 pictures people gathering indoors.
廿 (twenty) — a group of people meeting to measure or deliberate gave 度 its meaning of a 'degree' or 'measure,' as in temperature or angles.

example.pinyin: Jīntiān de tiānqì shì èrshí dù.
example.fact: 度 means 'degree,' used for temperature (二十度, 20 degrees) and angles, and also appears in 态度 (attitude).

etymologyHint: An open doorway or gate

components.note: 门 is a picture of a double-leafed door or gate, drawn symmetrically to show two swinging panels.

example.fact: 门 means 'door' or 'gate' and also serves as a category word, as in 专门 (specialized) and 部门 (department).

etymologyHint: person

components.note: 亻 (person) — 任 relates to a person taking on a responsibility or role.
壬 (rén) gives a hint of the sound — 任 is pronounced rèn, a connection that has shifted somewhat.

example.fact: 任 means 'to appoint' or 'responsibility,' appearing in 任务 (task, mission) and 任何 (any, whatsoever).

etymologyHint: cloth

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — 常 originally referred to a long skirt or banner made of cloth, later coming to mean something 'usual' or 'ordinary.'
尚 (shàng) gives a hint of the sound — 常 is pronounced cháng, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.english: He often goes to the library.
example.fact: 常 means 'often' or 'usual,' appearing in 常常 (often) and 平常 (usually, ordinary).

meanings: for the time being; for now
etymologyHint: Someone stepping 止 in front of another person 儿

components.note: 止 (a foot, stepping forward) — 先 pictures someone moving ahead of another.
儿 (a person) — one person stepping ahead of another gave 先 its meaning 'before' or 'first.'

example.fact: 先 means 'first' or 'before,' and 先生 (mister, literally 'born before,' i.e. senior) is the common polite title for men.

meanings: great number of people or things
etymologyHint: water

components.note: 氵 (water) — 海 relates to bodies of water, specifically the sea.
每 (měi) gives a hint of the sound — 海 is pronounced hǎi, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.english: Shanghai is in the eastern part of China.
example.fact: 海 means 'sea,' and 上海 (Shanghai, literally 'upon the sea') is one of China's largest and most famous coastal cities.

etymologyHint: walk

components.note: 辶 (to walk, movement) — 通 relates to passing through or getting somewhere.
甬 (yǒng) gives a hint of the sound — 通 is pronounced tōng, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.fact: 通 means 'to pass through' or 'connected,' appearing in 交通 (traffic, transportation) and 通过 (to pass through, to pass a test).

etymologyHint: script

components.note: 攵 (a hand with a stick) — 教 relates to instructing or disciplining, the traditional action of teaching.
孝 (xiào) gives a hint of the sound — 教 is pronounced jiào, a connection that has shifted somewhat.

example.english: The school's classroom is very big.
example.fact: 教 is pronounced jiào in words like 教室 (classroom) and 教育 (education), but pronounced jiāo when used alone as the verb 'to teach' (教英语, to teach English) — a common trap for learners.

etymologyHint: Simplified form of 兒, a picture of a child; compare 人

components.note: 儿 (simplified from 兒) depicts a small child, drawn with a large head on a small body — a simple picture of youth.

example.hanzi: 他有一个儿子和一个女儿。
example.pinyin: Tā yǒu yí gè érzi hé yí gè nǚ'ér.
example.english: He has a son and a daughter.
example.fact: 儿 means 'child' and appears in 儿子 (son) and 女儿 (daughter); it's also a common suffix added to nouns in northern Chinese speech, such as 花儿 (flower).

etymologyHint: cliff

components.note: 厂 (a cliff or overhang) — 原 relates to a source high up, such as a spring emerging from rock.
泉 (quán) gives a hint of the sound — 原 is pronounced yuán, a connection that has shifted somewhat.

example.pinyin: Nèi Měnggǔ yǒu hěn dà de cǎoyuán.
example.fact: 原 means 'source' or 'original,' and 草原 (grassland) refers to the vast grasslands found across Inner Mongolia and other parts of northern China.

meanings: host (i.e. sitting on east side of guest)
etymologyHint: Simplified form of 東, the sun 日 rising behind a tree 木

components.note: 东 (simplified from 東) originally pictured the sun 日 rising behind a tree 木 — since the sun rises in the east, the character came to mean 'east.'

example.english: The sun rises in the east.
example.fact: 东 means 'east' — the sun rises in the east (东) and sets in the west (西) everywhere on Earth.

etymologyHint: Simplified form of 聲; see that character for the etymology

components.note: 声 (simplified from 聲) refers to sound; the traditional form combined several elements related to hearing and music, simplified here into a more compact shape.

example.fact: 声 means 'sound' or 'voice' and appears in 声音 (sound) and 大声 (loudly).

meanings: used in 提防[di1 fang5] and 提溜[di1 liu5]
to carry (hanging down from the hand)
etymologyHint: hand

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 提 relates to lifting or carrying something by hand.
是 (shì) gives a hint of the sound — 提 is pronounced tí, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 他想提高自己的中文水平。
example.pinyin: Tā xiǎng tígāo zìjǐ de Zhōngwén shuǐpíng.
example.english: He wants to improve his Chinese level.
example.fact: 提 means 'to lift' or 'to raise,' appearing in 提高 (to raise, improve) and 提问 (to ask a question).

etymologyHint: A man standing on the ground 一

components.note: 立 depicts a person standing with arms and legs spread, on a horizontal line representing the ground — a simple picture of standing upright.

example.pinyin: Měiguó zài yī qī qī liù nián dúlì le.
example.fact: 立 means 'to stand' and appears in 独立 (independent, literally 'standing alone') and 立刻 (immediately).

example.pinyin: Tā huì shuō Zhōngwén yǐjí Yīngwén.
example.english: He can speak Chinese as well as English.
example.fact: 及 means 'and' or 'to reach,' most commonly seen in 以及 (as well as) and 来得及 (to make it in time).

etymologyHint: Two spoons 匕 side-by-side; 匕 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 比 is made of two identical 匕 (spoon) shapes placed side by side — comparing two similar things led to its meaning 'to compare.'

example.fact: 比 means 'to compare' and is used to form comparisons, similar to '-er than' in English — 比昨天冷 means 'colder than yesterday.'

meanings: (bound form) person engaged in a certain field of activity
etymologyHint: money

components.note: 贝 (shell/money — cowrie shells were historically used as currency) — 员 originally related to counting or officials responsible for accounts, later broadening to mean 'member' or 'personnel.'

example.english: Waiter, please give me the menu.
example.fact: 员 means 'member' or 'personnel' and appears in 服务员 (waiter/attendant) and 演员 (actor).

etymologyHint: To cut 刀 the horns 角 off of an ox 牛; 角 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 角 (horn) — 解 pictures removing a part of an animal.
牛 (ox) — together with a knife cutting between horn and ox, 解 pictures separating something into parts, giving its meaning 'to untie' or 'to explain.'

example.hanzi: 他帮我解决了这个问题。
example.pinyin: Tā bāng wǒ jiějué le zhège wèntí.
example.english: He helped me solve this problem.
example.fact: 解 means 'to untie' or 'to resolve,' appearing in 解决 (to solve/resolve) and 了解 (to understand).

etymologyHint: A river running between two banks; compare 川

components.note: 水 depicts a flowing stream, with a central current and ripples or drops branching off to the sides.

example.pinyin: Rén měitiān dōu yào hē shuǐ.
example.english: People need to drink water every day.
example.fact: 水 means 'water' and is one of the most fundamental characters in Chinese, appearing in countless words like 水果 (fruit) and 河水 (river water).

etymologyHint: A name called out 口 to hail someone at night 夕

components.note: 夕 (evening, night) — in the dark, one could not see a person's face, so calling out their name was necessary to identify them.
口 (mouth) — calling out with the mouth at night gave 名 its meaning 'name.'

example.fact: 名 means 'name' and 名字 (míngzi) is one of the very first words beginners learn to introduce themselves.

etymologyHint: A straight 直 (that is, level) table 几

components.note: 直 (straight, upright) — 真 relates to something level and true.
几 (a small table) — an object placed level and true on a table gave 真 its meaning 'real' or 'true.'

example.fact: 真 means 'true' or 'real,' and 真的 (zhēnde) is a very common way to say 'really' or confirm something is true.

meanings: abbr. for 論語|论语[Lun2 yu3], The Analects (of Confucius)
etymologyHint: Speech 讠 that explains the logic 仑; 仑 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 论 relates to discussing or explaining something with words.
仑 (logical order, arrangement) — combined with speech, 论 came to mean 'to discuss' or 'a theory,' explaining ideas in an orderly way.

example.hanzi: 我们在讨论今天的作业。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài tǎolùn jīntiān de zuòyè.
example.fact: 论 means 'to discuss' or 'theory,' appearing in 讨论 (to discuss) and 无论 (no matter what).

etymologyHint: To go somewhere 夂 and put down a flag 卜

components.note: 夂 (a foot, to go) — 处 relates to arriving somewhere.
卜 (a mark or flag) — planting a marker after arriving gave 处 its meaning of 'a place' or 'to settle, deal with.'

example.fact: 处 means 'place' or 'to handle/deal with,' appearing in 到处 (everywhere) and 好处 (benefit, advantage).

etymologyHint: Someone 土 stepping with their foot 止

components.note: 土 (here representing a person swinging their arms, not its usual meaning 'earth') — depicts someone in motion.
止 (a foot) — combined with the moving figure above, 走 shows a person walking or running.

example.fact: 走 means 'to walk' or 'to go,' and also forms 走路 (to walk, on foot).

meanings: (Tw) Italy (abbr. for 義大利|义大利[Yi4 da4 li4])
etymologyHint: sheep; simplified form of 義

components.note: ⺷ (sheep, related to 羊) — 义 relates to what is right or moral, linked to the idea of sacrificial sheep used in rituals of righteousness.
乂 (yì) gives the sound — 义 is also pronounced yì, an exact match.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì hěn yǒu yìyì.
example.fact: 义 means 'righteousness' or 'meaning,' appearing in 意义 (meaning, significance) and 正义 (justice).

etymologyHint: Walking 夂 and talking 口

components.note: 夂 (a foot, to walk) — 各 pictures people arriving from different directions.
口 (mouth) — different people speaking gave 各 its meaning 'each' or 'every,' emphasizing individual distinctness.

example.pinyin: Shāngdiàn lǐ yǒu gè zhǒng shuǐguǒ.
example.english: The store has all kinds of fruit.
example.fact: 各 means 'each' or 'every,' appearing in 各种 (various kinds) and 各自 (each one, respectively).

meanings: to join; to become a member of
(bound form) to conform to (as in 入時|入时[ru4 shi2])
etymologyHint: An arrow indicating "enter"

components.note: 入 depicts a simple wedge or arrow shape pointing inward, showing the direction of entering.

example.fact: 入 means 'to enter' and appears in 入口 (entrance) and 进入 (to enter).

etymologyHint: A small table; compare 丌

components.note: 几 depicts a small low table or stool with legs — a simple domestic object.

example.pinyin: Nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ gè rén?
example.english: How many people are in your family?
example.fact: 几 is used to ask 'how many' for numbers usually under ten, as in 几个人 (how many people), while 多少 is used for larger or unknown quantities.

meanings: classifier for things with mouths (people, domestic animals, cannons, wells etc)
etymologyHint: An open mouth

components.note: 口 is a simple picture of an open mouth.

example.fact: 口 means 'mouth' and also forms 人口 (population, literally 'person-mouths'), reflecting how a household's size was once counted by mouths to feed.

etymologyHint: speech

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 认 relates to recognizing or acknowledging something, often expressed through words.
人 (rén) gives the sound — 认 is pronounced rèn, a close variant of the same sound.

example.fact: 认 means 'to recognize,' and 认识 (rènshi, to know/be acquainted with) is one of the very first verbs beginners learn when meeting new people.

example.pinyin: Hé lǐ yǒu yì tiáo yú.
example.english: There is a fish in the river.
example.fact: 条 is a measure word for long, thin things, such as 一条路 (a road), 一条鱼 (a fish), and 一条裤子 (a pair of pants).

etymologyHint: A leveling scale

components.note: 平 depicts a balance scale drawn level and symmetrical — a simple picture of flatness and equality.

example.fact: 平 means 'flat' or 'even,' and 和平 (peace) combines it with 和 (harmony) to describe a calm, balanced world.

etymologyHint: thread

components.note: 糸 (thread/silk) — 系 relates to connecting or tying things together, like threads linking into a system.

example.fact: 系 means 'to connect' or 'a system,' appearing in 关系 (relationship) and, in universities, 系 also means 'department.'

etymologyHint: A person 亻 breathing air

components.note: 气 (simplified from 氣) depicts rising wisps or vapor, like breath or steam drifting upward — a simple picture of air or gas.

example.fact: 气 means 'air' or 'gas,' appearing in 天气 (weather, literally 'sky air') and 生气 (to be angry, literally 'to generate energy').

etymologyHint: head

components.note: 页 (head/page) — 题 relates to the forehead or the topmost part, extending to the 'title' or 'topic' placed at the top.
是 (shì) gives a hint of the sound — 题 is pronounced tí, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.pinyin: Lǎoshī wèn le yí gè wèntí.
example.fact: 题 means 'topic' or 'question,' appearing in 问题 (question, problem) and 题目 (title, topic).

etymologyHint: water

components.note: 氵 (water) — 活 relates to water flowing, a symbol of life and vitality.
舌 (shé) gives a hint of the sound — 活 is pronounced huó, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.fact: 活 means 'alive' or 'to live,' appearing in 生活 (life, daily living) and 活动 (activity, event).
尔 was a classical word for 'you'; today it mainly survives in words like 偶尔 (occasionally) and in transliterations of foreign names.

meanings: one of the five two-hour periods into which the night was formerly divided

example.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.
example.fact: 更 means 'even more,' used to strengthen comparisons — 更冷 means 'even colder.'

etymologyHint: To draw boundaries 刂 between classes 另

components.note: 另 (other, separate) — 别 relates to distinguishing one thing from another.
刂 (knife) — cutting things apart to sort them gave 别 its meaning 'to separate' or 'other,' and later, 'don't' as a command.

example.fact: 别 is commonly used to mean 'don't,' as in 别担心 (don't worry) and 别哭 (don't cry).

etymologyHint: hand

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.

example.fact: 打 literally means 'to hit,' but it combines with many words for varied actions, such as 打电话 (to make a phone call) and 打篮球 (to play basketball).

etymologyHint: A woman turned to the side

components.note: 女 depicts a kneeling figure with arms crossed, a traditional posture — a simple picture of a woman.

example.fact: 女 means 'female' or 'woman,' appearing in 女儿 (daughter) and 女人 (woman).
变 means 'to change' and appears in 变化 (change) and 变成 (to become, turn into).

etymologyHint: A child 儿 in a room with four walls 囗

components.note: 囗 (an enclosure) — 四 pictures a bounded space.
儿 (a person) — a person enclosed within four walls gave 四 its meaning 'four,' though the exact link to the number is debated.

example.pinyin: Yì nián yǒu sì gè jìjié.
example.fact: 四 means 'four' — a year is divided into four seasons: spring, summer, autumn, and winter.

etymologyHint: spirit

components.note: 礻 (an altar, related to ritual/spirits) — 神 relates to gods and spirits.
申 (shēn) gives a hint of the sound — 神 is pronounced shén, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.fact: 神 means 'god' or 'spirit,' appearing in 精神 (spirit, energy) and 神话 (myth, literally 'spirit story').

etymologyHint: Many mouths 口 speaking with one mind 心

components.note: 口 (mouths) — 总 pictures many voices.
心 (heart, mind) — many mouths brought together under one mind gave 总 its meaning 'overall' or 'to gather together.'

example.fact: 总 means 'overall' or 'always,' appearing in 总是 (always) and 总共 (in total, altogether).

example.english: He doesn't know how to answer.
example.fact: 何 is a formal word for 'what' or 'how,' often seen in 如何 (how) and 为何 (why); in everyday speech, 什么 and 怎么 are used instead.

meanings: to get (or give) an electric shock
etymologyHint: Simplified form of 電; lightning 申 from a storm cloud 雨

components.note: 电 (simplified from 電) depicts a bolt of lightning — since lightning is a natural form of electricity, the character came to mean 'electricity.'

example.english: I use a computer to do homework.
example.fact: 电 means 'electricity,' originally depicting lightning; it now appears in modern words like 电脑 (computer) and 电视 (television).

meanings: to count as; to regard as
etymologyHint: script

components.note: 攵 (a hand with a stick, action) — 数 relates to the action of counting.
娄 (lóu) gives a hint of the sound — 数 is pronounced shù, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.fact: 数 means 'number' or 'to count,' appearing in 数字 (number, digit) and 数学 (mathematics).

meanings: to calm; to set at ease
etymologyHint: A woman 女 safe in a house 宀

components.note: 宀 (a roof, house) — 安 pictures shelter.
女 (woman) — a woman safely inside a house gave 安 its meaning 'peace' or 'safety.'

example.hanzi: 开车的时候要注意安全。
example.pinyin: Kāichē de shíhou yào zhùyì ānquán.
example.english: You should pay attention to safety while driving.
example.fact: 安 means 'peace' or 'safe,' appearing in 安全 (safe, safety) and 平安 (peace, well-being).

etymologyHint: Grains of sand; 小 provides the pronunciation and meaning

components.note: 少 depicts a few small dots or grains, like scattered sand — a simple picture of a small quantity, giving the meaning 'few' or 'little.'

example.english: There are very few people here.
example.fact: 少 means 'few' or 'little,' and 多少 (duōshao) asks 'how many/much,' combining 多 (many) and 少 (few).

meanings: to report; to inform; to announce
to sign up for; to register for (abbr. for 報名|报名[bao4 ming2])
etymologyHint: A hand 扌 cuffing 又 a criminal 卩, representing sentencing

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 报 relates to taking action against someone.
卩 (a kneeling or bound person) — handling a wrongdoer and announcing the judgment gave 报 its meaning 'to report' or 'to announce.'

example.english: Dad reads the newspaper every day.
example.fact: 报 means 'to report' or 'newspaper,' appearing in 报纸 (newspaper) and 报名 (to sign up, literally 'to report one's name').

etymologyHint: A sprout growing in the ground, representing a budding talent

components.note: 才 depicts a young sprout just breaking through the soil — new growth came to represent budding talent or ability.

example.fact: 才 can mean 'just now' (刚才) or 'talent' (人才, a talented person), and is also used to mean 'only then,' showing something happens later than expected.

meanings: (of a plant) to produce (fruit or seeds)
etymologyHint: thread

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 结 relates to tying or knotting threads together.
吉 (jí) gives a hint of the sound — 结 is pronounced jié, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.fact: 结 means 'to tie' or 'to conclude,' appearing in 结婚 (to marry, literally 'to tie together') and 结束 (to end, finish).

etymologyHint: A hand 又 held up against a cliff 厂

components.note: 厂 (a cliff or overhang) — 反 pictures pushing against a steep surface.
又 (a hand) — a hand pushing back against a cliff gave 反 its meaning 'to turn over' or 'opposite.'

example.fact: 反 means 'opposite' or 'to oppose,' appearing in 反对 (to oppose) and 相反 (opposite, contrary).

etymologyHint: Something 冖 passed from one hand 爫 to another 又

components.note: 爫 (a hand, from above) — 受 pictures something being passed.
又 (a hand, from below) — one hand giving and another receiving gave 受 its meaning 'to receive' or 'to endure.'

example.fact: 受 means 'to receive,' appearing in 接受 (to accept) and 受到 (to receive, to be subjected to).

etymologyHint: An eye drawn on its side

components.note: 目 depicts an eye turned on its side, with the outline and pupil visible — later straightened into today's rectangular shape.

example.fact: 目 means 'eye,' and by extension, 'goal' — 目的 (goal, purpose) and 节目 (program, show) both derive from this character.

etymologyHint: A giant 大 with a normal-sized man 丶 for scale

components.note: 太 adds a small dot below 大 (big) — the extra mark emphasizes something even bigger or more extreme, giving 太 its meaning 'too' or 'extremely.'

example.fact: 太 means 'too' or 'extremely' when placed before an adjective (太热, too hot), and also appears in 太阳 (the sun).

etymologyHint: unit

components.note: 里 (a unit of distance, related to a village measure) — 量 relates to measuring quantity.
旦 (dàn) gives a hint of the sound — 量 is pronounced liàng, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.

example.fact: 量 means 'quantity' or 'amount,' appearing in 数量 (quantity) and 力量 (strength, force).

meanings: further; beyond this point of time
etymologyHint: Two fish 冉 caught on a line 一

components.note: 再 depicts something stacked again on top of a base line — repetition, or doing something 'once more,' is pictured by piling on an extra layer.

example.fact: 再 means 'again' or 'once more,' appearing in 再见 (goodbye, literally 'see again') and 再说一次 (say it again).

etymologyHint: Two hearts 心 beating together 咸

components.note: 咸 (all, together) — 感 relates to a shared reaction.
心 (heart) — feelings that stir the heart gave 感 its meaning 'to feel' or 'emotion.'

example.english: Thank you very much for your help.
example.fact: 感 means 'to feel,' appearing in 感觉 (to feel, sense) and 感谢 (to thank, be grateful).

etymologyHint: action

components.note: 廴 (to move forward, extend) — 建 relates to constructing or setting something up over an extended process.
聿 (yù) gives a hint of the sound — 建 is pronounced jiàn, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 长城是两千多年前建的。
example.pinyin: Chángchéng shì liǎng qiān duō nián qián jiàn de.
example.english: The Great Wall was built more than 2,000 years ago.
example.fact: 建 means 'to build' or 'to establish,' and 长城 (the Great Wall) began being built more than 2,000 years ago.

example.english: The waiter's service is very good.
example.fact: 务 relates to tasks and duties, appearing in 任务 (task, mission) and 服务 (service).

meanings: to do; to engage in; to hold (a party etc)
etymologyHint: Someone 亻 who causes things to happen 故; 故 also provides the pronuncation

components.note: 亻 (person) — 做 relates to a person carrying out an action.
故 (cause, reason, to happen) — combined with 亻 (person), 做 came to mean 'to make' or 'to do,' someone actively causing something to happen.

example.fact: 做 means 'to do' or 'to make,' one of the most versatile verbs in Chinese, as in 做饭 (to cook) and 做作业 (to do homework).

etymologyHint: hand

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 接 relates to receiving or connecting something by hand.
妾 (qiè) gives a hint of the sound — 接 is pronounced jiē, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.english: Mom went to the airport to pick me up.
example.fact: 接 means 'to receive' or 'to meet/pick up,' appearing in 接受 (to accept) and 接机 (to pick someone up at the airport).
必 means 'must' and most often appears in 必须 (bìxū, must, have to).

meanings: classifier for events and happenings: spell, episode, bout
large place used for a specific purpose
etymologyHint: earth

components.note: 土 (earth) — 场 relates to a flat open area of ground, such as a field or venue.
昜 (yáng) gives a hint of the sound — 场 is pronounced chǎng, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.

example.pinyin: Zhège shìchǎng mài hěn duō shuǐguǒ.
example.english: This market sells a lot of fruit.
example.fact: 场 means 'a place, field, or venue,' appearing in 机场 (airport), 市场 (market), and 广场 (public square).

meanings: classifier for events, things, clothes etc
etymologyHint: A man 亻 dividing up a cow 牛

components.note: 亻 (person) — 件 relates to a person separating something into parts.
牛 (ox) — dividing an ox into pieces gave 件 its meaning of an individual 'item' or 'piece,' now used as a measure word for objects and matters.

example.pinyin: Tā mǎi le yí jiàn xīn yīfu.
example.english: She bought a new piece of clothing.
example.fact: 件 is a measure word for individual items or matters, such as 一件衣服 (a piece of clothing) and 一件事 (a matter, an affair).

etymologyHint: speech

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 计 relates to counting or planning through words and numbers.
十 (shí) gives a hint of the sound — 计 is pronounced jì, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen yǒu yí gè lǚxíng jìhuà.
example.fact: 计 means 'to plan' or 'to calculate,' appearing in 计划 (plan) and 计算 (to calculate).

etymologyHint: bamboo

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — 管 originally referred to a bamboo pipe or tube, later broadening to mean 'to manage' or 'to control.'
官 (guān) gives a hint of the sound — 管 is pronounced guǎn, a connection that has shifted only slightly in tone.

example.fact: 管 originally meant a bamboo pipe, and later came to mean 'to manage' or 'to be in charge of,' as in 管理 (to manage).

etymologyHint: moon

components.note: 月 (moon) — 期 relates to time measured by the moon's cycles, like a period or term.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 期 is pronounced qī, a connection that has shifted slightly in tone.

example.english: I am very busy this semester.
example.fact: 期 relates to a period of time, and 星期 (week) is literally 'star period,' since ancient astronomers linked the seven-day cycle to celestial bodies.

example.hanzi: 上海是中国最大的城市。
example.pinyin: Shànghǎi shì Zhōngguó zuì dà de chéngshì.
example.fact: 市 means 'city' or 'market,' and 上海 is the largest city in China by population.

meanings: Zhi (c. 2000 BC), fifth of the legendary Flame Emperors 炎帝[Yan2 di4] descended from Shennong 神農|神农[Shen2 nong2] Farmer God
etymologyHint: To look someone in the eye 目

components.note: 十 (here a straight vertical line) — 直 pictures something drawn perfectly straight.
目 (eye) — looking directly and steadily with the eye gave 直 its meaning 'straight' or 'direct.'

example.english: He has always lived in Beijing.
example.fact: 直 means 'straight' or 'direct,' appearing in 一直 (always, continuously) and 直接 (direct, directly).

meanings: abbr. for 德國|德国[De2 guo2]
etymologyHint: heart

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 德 relates to inner moral character and virtue.

example.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè yǒu dàodé de rén.
example.english: He is a person with good morals.
example.fact: 德 means 'virtue' or 'morality' (道德), and is also used to abbreviate 德国 (Germany).

etymologyHint: money

components.note: 贝 (shell/money) — 资 relates to wealth, funds, and resources.
次 (cì) gives a hint of the sound — 资 is pronounced zī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.

example.fact: 资 relates to money and resources, appearing in 工资 (salary/wages) and 投资 (to invest).

etymologyHint: An order 令 given by mouth 口

components.note: 令 (an order, command) — 命 pictures issuing a command.
口 (mouth) — a command given aloud gave 命 its meaning 'order' or 'decree,' and by extension, 'fate' or 'life.'

example.pinyin: Měi gè shēngmìng dōu hěn zhēnguì.
example.fact: 命 originally meant 'order' or 'decree,' and later came to mean 'fate' or 'life,' as in 生命 (life) and 命令 (a command).

meanings: (coll.) small bundle of straw for silkworms to spin cocoons on
etymologyHint: Three mountain peaks

components.note: 山 is a simple picture of three mountain peaks in a row.

example.pinyin: Tàishān shì Zhōngguó yǒumíng de shān.
example.english: Mount Tai is a famous mountain in China.
example.fact: 山 means 'mountain,' and 泰山 (Mount Tai) is one of China's most sacred and famous mountains, historically climbed by emperors.

etymologyHint: A cast-iron bell

components.note: 金 depicts a bell or metal casting mold, with dots representing droplets of molten metal — a picture linked to metal and, later, specifically gold.

example.english: This ring is made of gold.
example.fact: 金 means 'gold' or 'metal,' appearing in 现金 (cash) and as a common syllable in words related to metal.

etymologyHint: To point 旨 by hand 扌; 旨 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 指 relates to using the hand, specifically the fingers.
旨 (an aim, purpose) — combined with 扌 (hand), 指 came to mean 'finger' and 'to point,' aiming the hand at something.

example.english: He points at the map with his finger.
example.fact: 指 means 'finger' or 'to point,' appearing in 手指 (finger) and 指路 (to point out directions).

meanings: abbr. for 克羅地亞|克罗地亚[Ke4 luo2 di4 ya4], Croatia
(Tw) abbr. for 克羅埃西亞|克罗埃西亚[Ke4 luo2 ai1 xi1 ya4], Croatia
etymologyHint: A weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄

components.note: 十 (here representing a weapon or armor) — 克 pictures overcoming an opponent.
兄 (a person, here representing a formidable figure) — overcoming a strong opponent gave 克 its meaning 'to overcome' or 'to be able to.'

example.pinyin: Zhège píngguǒ yǒu liǎng bǎi kè.
example.fact: 克 is the standard unit for grams in the metric system, and separately means 'to overcome,' as in 克服 (to overcome a difficulty).

etymologyHint: speech

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 许 relates to giving permission through words.
午 (wǔ) gives a hint of the sound — 许 is pronounced xǔ, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.

example.english: The teacher allowed us to go out and play.
example.fact: 许 means 'to permit,' appearing in 允许 (to allow, permit) and 也许 (maybe, perhaps).

etymologyHint: thread

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 统 relates to threads gathered into one continuous strand, extending to the idea of unifying or governing as one system.
充 (chōng) gives a hint of the sound — 统 is pronounced tǒng, a connection that has shifted somewhat.

example.fact: 统 means 'to unify' or 'a system,' and 秦始皇 (Qin Shi Huang) was the first emperor to unify China, in 221 BC.

etymologyHint: A place 匸 under a lord's control 乂

components.note: 匸 (an enclosure or boundary) — 区 pictures a defined territory.
乂 (a mark, here representing control or division) — dividing land into bounded territories gave 区 its meaning 'district' or 'area.'

example.pinyin: Tā zhù zài yí gè xīn de xiǎoqū.
example.english: He lives in a new residential community.
example.fact: 区 means 'area' or 'district,' appearing in 地区 (region) and 小区 (residential community, neighborhood).

meanings: Bulgaria (abbr. for 保加利亞|保加利亚[Bao3 jia1 li4 ya4])
to defend; to protect; to keep
etymologyHint: person

components.note: 亻 (person) — 保 relates to a person looking after or protecting someone, originally a caretaker holding a child.
呆 (dāi) gives a hint of the sound — 保 is pronounced bǎo, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.fact: 保 means 'to protect,' appearing in 保护 (to protect) and 保证 (to guarantee).

etymologyHint: A bird alighting on the ground 土

components.note: 至 depicts an arrow reaching the ground after landing — arriving at a destination gave 至 its meaning 'to arrive' or 'until.'

example.hanzi: 他甚至不知道我的名字。
example.pinyin: Tā shènzhì bù zhīdào wǒ de míngzi.
example.english: He doesn't even know my name.
example.fact: 至 means 'to arrive' or 'until,' appearing in 甚至 (even, to the extent that) and 直到 (until).

etymologyHint: A group of people 人 gathered in one place 阝

components.note: 阝 (a mound or place) — 队 pictures people gathering together.
人 (person) — people gathering in one place gave 队 its meaning 'a team' or 'a line/queue.'

example.pinyin: Mǎi piào de rén dōu zài páiduì.
example.english: People buying tickets are all lining up.
example.fact: 队 means 'team' or 'line,' appearing in 排队 (to line up, queue) and 球队 (sports team).

etymologyHint: Sunlight 彡 streaming through a window 开

components.note: 开 (open, here representing a frame or opening) — 形 pictures light passing through a gap.
彡 (streaks or rays of light) — light and pattern coming through an opening gave 形 its meaning 'shape' or 'form.'

example.hanzi: 这个盒子的形状是圆的。
example.pinyin: Zhège hézi de xíngzhuàng shì yuán de.
example.english: The shape of this box is round.
example.fact: 形 means 'shape' or 'form,' appearing in 形状 (shape) and 情形 (situation, circumstance).

meanings: god of the soil and altars to him
etymologyHint: An earth 土 spirit 礻; 礻 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 礻 (an altar, related to ritual) — 社 relates to worship and community gatherings.
土 (earth) — ancient communities worshipped a local earth spirit together, giving 社 its meaning 'society' or 'community.'

example.fact: 社 originally referred to worshipping a local earth spirit, and later came to mean 'society' or 'community,' as in 社会 (society) and 社区 (community).
便 means 'convenient,' most often seen in 方便 (fāngbiàn, convenient), and also means 'then' in formal writing.

etymologyHint: cave

components.note: 穴 (a cave/hole) — 空 relates to an empty hollow space.
工 (gōng) gives a hint of the sound — 空 is pronounced kōng, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.fact: 空 means 'empty' or 'sky,' appearing in 天空 (sky) and 空气 (air).

example.english: He decided to study abroad in China.
example.fact: 决 means 'to decide,' most often appearing in 决定 (juédìng, to decide, a decision).

etymologyHint: A structure 台 that directs the flow of water 氵

components.note: 氵 (water) — 治 relates to managing or controlling the flow of water, such as flood control.
台 (a platform, structure) — a structure used to direct and control water gave 治 its meaning 'to govern' or 'to manage.'

example.fact: 治 means 'to govern' or 'to treat/cure,' appearing in 政治 (politics) and 治病 (to treat an illness).

etymologyHint: Laying out clothes 㠭 for sale in a market 尸; compare 㠭

components.note: 尸 (here representing a covering or stall, not a corpse) — 展 pictures a place where goods are displayed.
衣 (clothing) — clothing laid out for display gave 展 its meaning 'to unfold' or 'to exhibit.'

example.pinyin: Zhōngguó de jīngjì fāzhǎn hěn kuài.
example.fact: 展 means 'to unfold' or 'to display,' appearing in 发展 (to develop) and 展览 (exhibition).

meanings: abbr. for Malaysia 馬來西亞|马来西亚[Ma3 lai2 xi1 ya4]
etymologyHint: Simplified form of 馬, a horse galloping to the left

components.note: 马 (simplified from 馬) depicts a horse in profile, with its mane, legs, and tail visible — later simplified into just a few strokes.

example.pinyin: Gǔdài rén yòng mǎ lái lǚxíng.
example.english: Ancient people used horses to travel.
example.fact: 马 means 'horse' — before cars and trains, horses were one of the main ways people and goods traveled long distances in ancient China.

etymologyHint: A hand measuring 斗 grain 禾

components.note: 禾 (grain, a rice/wheat plant) — 科 relates to sorting and measuring crops.
斗 (a measuring ladle) — measuring grain into ordered categories gave 科 its meaning 'a branch of study' or 'a department.'

example.pinyin: Tā duì kēxué hěn gǎn xìngqù.
example.english: He is very interested in science.
example.fact: 科 means 'a branch of study,' appearing in 科学 (science) and 学科 (academic subject).

etymologyHint: A person speaking orders 口 and raising their arm

components.note: 司 depicts a person with a raised arm giving orders — an official directing others, giving rise to the meaning 'to manage' or 'to take charge of.'

example.pinyin: Tā zài yì jiā dà gōngsī gōngzuò.
example.english: He works at a big company.
example.fact: 司 means 'to manage' or 'to take charge,' and most often appears today in 公司 (company).

etymologyHint: Five elements (the cross with the extra stroke) between heaven 一 and earth 一

components.note: 五 places an X-shaped cross between two horizontal lines representing heaven and earth — in traditional cosmology, this was linked to the five elements that fill the space between.

example.hanzi: 中国传统文化有五种元素:金、木、水、火、土。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó chuántǒng wénhuà yǒu wǔ zhǒng yuánsù: jīn, mù, shuǐ, huǒ, tǔ.
example.english: Traditional Chinese culture has five elements: metal, wood, water, fire, and earth.
example.fact: 五 means 'five,' and in traditional Chinese thought, the number five is linked to five basic elements: metal, wood, water, fire, and earth.

meanings: (bound form) gay (loanword from English into Cantonese, Jyutping: gei1, followed by orthographic borrowing from Cantonese)
etymologyHint: earth

components.note: 土 (earth) — 基 relates to the ground or foundation something is built on.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 基 is pronounced jī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.

example.english: Laying a good foundation is very important.
example.fact: 基 means 'foundation' or 'base,' appearing in 基础 (foundation, basics) and 基本 (basic, fundamental).
